title: Christmas Eve Roast Beef
headnote: The star of Christmas Eve dinner and a family favorite. “Getting to 120 degrees in the thickest part of the meat usually takes about 15 minutes per pound when the oven is at 350 degrees. 1 rib bone can usually feed two people.” — Bob Mitchell

quotes.text: Getting to 120 degrees in the thickest part of the meat usually takes about 15 minutes per pound when the oven is at 350 degrees. 1 rib bone can usually feed two people.
quotes.span: “Getting to 120 degrees in the thickest part of the meat usually takes about 15 minutes per pound when the oven is at 350 degrees. 1 rib bone can usually feed two people.” — Bob Mitchell

items.raw: 1 bone-in rib roast — 4 ribs (about 8 pounds) for 8 people; 1 rib feeds about 2. Linda prefers it boned and tied back onto the bones (ask the butcher).
2 tablespoons kosher salt — “lots and lots of salt”

steps.text: Let the roast sit on the counter for at least one hour.
Heat the oven to 450°F with a rack in the lower third. Set the meat in a proper roasting pan with the ribs facing down.
Cut the garlic cloves into halves or thirds. Stab the roast all over with a paring knife and gently insert the garlic pieces into the cuts, so you do not tear up the shape of the meat.
Season the entire outside generously with lots and lots of salt and freshly ground pepper.
Roast in the lower third of the oven at 450°F for about 20 minutes to build a deep brown crust.

Lower the oven to 350°F and keep roasting, rotating the pan 2 or 3 times for even browning, until the thickest part reads 120°F for medium-rare — about 15 minutes per pound, so roughly 2 hours for an 8-pound roast. Start checking early.
Take it out of the oven and cover loosely with foil for 15 to 20 minutes. The temperature will rise another 10 to 15°F as it rests.

While it rests, pour off all but 2 tablespoons of fat, set the pan over medium heat, add the stock and wine, and scrape up the browned bits; simmer 5 minutes and season. Snip the strings (or cut along the bones), lift the meat off the bones, slice, and serve with the jus.

notes.label: Linda’s way
notes.text: she prefers the roast boned, then tied back onto the bones to roast. You get the flavor and the built-in rack of the bones, and carving is just snipping the strings.

notes.label: Doneness, pulled from the oven
notes.text: rare 115°F, medium-rare 120°F, medium 130°F. A probe thermometer left in the meat takes the guessing out.

notes.label: First-draft herb version
notes.text: mash 6 minced garlic cloves with 2 tablespoons each chopped rosemary and thyme and 2 tablespoons olive oil, and rub it over the roast before searing. It works alongside Bob’s garlic studding.

notes.label: Alongside
notes.text: the Holiday Scalloped Potatoes in Chapter 9.

openQuestion: Bob’s recipe card calls this “Garlic-Studded Roast Beef.” Is it the Christmas Eve roast?
lindasTouchReason: Linda likes it boned and tied back on
